case_name: Mohit Goyal vs State Of Uttarakhand

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Mohit Goyal, husband; Satish Kumar Goyal, father-in-law; Smt. Anshu Goyal, mother-in-law; Anjali, married sister-in-law; Manoj Kumar, brother-in-law
parties.respondent_defendant: State of Uttarakhand, Principal Secretary Home; S.H.O., Police Station Jwalapur; Priyanka, wife

facts_of_case: Petitioners sought quashing of First Information Report No. 37 of 2013 relating to offences punishable under section 498A of IPC and one punishable under section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

legal_principles.principle: Abuse of process of law is not permitted.
legal_principles.held: It is argued that it is abuse of process of law on the part of the respondent no.3 to implicate the entire family members of her husband due to their matrimonial discord.

legal_principles.principle: A party cannot use the process of law to harass or intimidate others.
legal_principles.held: It is contended that after the petitioner no.1 filed divorce petition against the respondent no.3 as a counter blast the respondent no.3 filed not only a petition under section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act, and application under section 125 of Cr.P.C, but also got lodged the impugned First Information Report.

outcome.final_order: Urgency Application No. 860 of 2013 is allowed.

use_for_drafting: seeking interim relief in matrimonial disputes
